direction.premise: Last light in a collapsed medieval abbey: the player's sweeping flame reveals architecture and burns shadows.
direction.composition: Edge-to-edge moonlit floor and glowing center reliquary; thin status on stage and wooden bell console below.
direction.shapeLanguage: Pixel glyph creatures with sharp long cloaks, antlers and segmented wings; heavy architectural sides, angular standing stones.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Weathered lime masonry, carved stone circles, dark verdigris brass, warm analog glass flare over strict integer sprites.
direction.paletteLogic: Charcoal and muted jade for ground/enemies; ceramic off-white for information; isolated gold/terracotta for flame and real damage.
direction.typography: Narrow engraved serif game logo, restrained system captions for urgent status only.
direction.signature: A rotating cone of light physically cuts through the enemy silhouettes and reveals the forgotten abbey as the player drags.
direction.distinction: Not a side-view arena cabinet, not an all-over green garden miniature, and not a colorful tool tray.
direction.spatialRationale: Arena owns all remaining phone height. Control is direct within it; one large bell button in the bottom strip, no scrolling.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Horizontal head/altar/bronze console composition contains an orthographic enclosed ground circle rather than a vertical open-air mechanical pilgrimage.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Moving light and a timed bell defend the tower against autonomous enemies rather than selecting walking supports.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Full vertical top-down floor instead of landscape fighting cabinet.
comparisons.interactionDifference: One sweeping aim gesture and timed pulse instead of a set of individual fighter buttons.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Stone lit battlefield without brush tray or pastel stamps.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Drag changes the beam and battle rather than leaving image stamps.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Dark lantern reliquary floor instead of golf greenery.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Survival wave pressure rather than physics putts.

production.renderer: Single 2D canvas with exact 32px pixel source, generated PNG atlas, vector engraved PWA seal and render-time luminous falloff.
production.focalAsset: Deterministically authored creature frames with 14-color palette and fixed 32x32 cell and pivot.

motion.character: Weighted imperceptible sprite rocking, clear impact flashes and candle drift; no endless bounce on UI.
motion.action: Pointer turns the lamp continuously; button sounds a bronze chime.
motion.anticipation: Warm beam makes hostile approach visible before they reach the reliquary.
motion.response: Exposure reduces enemy health every fixed-time update; bell instantly damages and knocks enemies outward.
motion.followThrough: Dying shadows shatter into embers; bell ring expands across the stone floor.
motion.interruption: Pause freezes enemy simulation; reduced-motion removes shake but preserves legible hits.
motion.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion disables incidental camera shake and CSS transitions.

evidence.expectedChange: The initial overlay closes, wave I spawns playable enemies and bell input becomes active.

architecture.primaryVerb: Aim the oil lamp by dragging a pointer, exposing and destroying oncoming shadows.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Beam turns instantly, enemies flash, sparks shed and HP decreases; timed bell pushes enemies out in a visible ring.
architecture.spatialRationale: Portrait mobile stage fills available height between tiny safe-area header and bell console; controls never need scrolling.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Two small fixed structural strips contain an interactive circular abbey floor and bronze bell; unlike PALOMNIK's unframed sky-filling side-view walking fortress and floating stepping stones.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous thumb-controlled rotating lantern beam and timed area pulse burn enemies, rather than discrete taps to move a giant machine between rock supports.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Vertical medieval light-well with minimal header and physical bell slab, unlike horizontal plush platform scenery with an extensive motion pad.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Finger selects lantern beam angle while the central reliquary stays fixed, instead of pushing and jumping a plush body.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A carved nocturnal stone circle organized around one stationary sacred object, not a co-op mobile field marked by moving heroes and rope.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Rotating directional light and timed area pulses, not moving a rope-linked character around obstacles.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Immersive textured circular battlefield replaces open square drawing canvas and tool row.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous aiming affects moving attackers rather than adding stamps.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Kinetic illuminated arena replaces any document-like ritual choices.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Realtime wave survival replaces sequential decisions.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Physical tower and shadow floor replaces framed paintings.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Drag controls destructive light, not painting restoration.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Portrait top-down world instead of wide two-character fighter cabinet.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Aim-and-bell replaces several attack and movement buttons.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Cyclic stone arena instead of an irregular putting course.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Light damage over time replaces ball strike physics.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Black Bazaar arranges bid forms and hidden trading balances in an inventory workspace; Pepelny Dozor displays a single full-height circular stone arena with physically controlled flame.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Black Bazaar participants submit market orders with protected inventory, Pepelny Dozor rotates light and rings a defensive bell against real-time shadow attackers.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Picto uses light paper with semantic stamp panels and a story composition strip; Pepelny Dozor presents pixel-art enemies, an abbey floor and a luminous directional beam.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Picto players draw and guess symbol stories asynchronously by turn; Pepelny Dozor directly aims a damage-causing light cone in an active wave.
